newsitem.title: USA: Coors posts record profits and barrel sales.
newsitem.headline: Coors posts record profits and barrel sales.

text.p: Adolph Coors Co. said Thursday that its profits more than doubled in the second quarter to a record $51 million as the number of barrels of beer it sold hit a new high.
The brewer said its net income for the 13 weeks ended June 29 rose to a record $51.0 million, or $1.36 a share, from $23.8 million, or 63 cents a share.
Excluding special items, earnings per share were 97 cents, well above the 71 cents anticipated by Wall Street, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
Coors stock shot up $1 to $28.625 in morning trading on the Nasdaq market, surpassing its 52-week high of $28.375.
Coors said sales grew 3.1 percent to $520 million from $505 million, as the number of barrels of beer and other malt beverages sold edged up to a record 5.81 million from 5.79 million.
The company said its second-quarter results included a net special credit of $14.6 million, or 39 cents a share.

The credit included a $71.5 million payment from Molson Breweries to settle legal disputes (less legal expenses), which was offset by $22.4 million reserve related to an investment in South Korea and a $14.4 million charge related to an underperforming brewery in Spain.
For the first half of the year Coors said its net income climbed to $59.1 million, or $1.57 a share, from $20.8 million, or 55 cents a share, in the first half of 1996.
It said sales hit a record $919.8 million, up 4.9 percent from $876.8 million a year earlier.
Sales volume reached a record 10.3 million barrels, up 2.4 percent from 10.1 million barrels a year earlier.
